body:
## Summary

A knowledge triple's subject, predicate, and object are stored as **plaintext** in the `triples` table, even though the identical content is correctly DEK-sealed inside the carrier item's `content_ciphertext`.

The compliance erasure path never references the `triples` table. So a verified data-subject erasure destroys the DEK — correctly rendering the carrier item unreadable — while the same content sits in the clear in a neighbouring table and remains fully readable with no key.

The result: the system writes a tombstone, passes its own DEK-destruction verification probe, and records the erasure as successful, while the content is still readable. That is a false attestation of erasure in the project's own audit trail.

**Severity: High.** Confidentiality loss at rest plus a compliance/erasure failure.

## Affected code

| Location | Role |
|---|---|
| `sql/001_core.sql:236-238` | `triples.subject`, `triples.predicate`, `triples.object` are plain `text NOT NULL` columns |
| `crates/clio-store/src/sqlite_triple.rs:158-186` | inserts the SPO verbatim into those columns |
| `crates/clio-store/src/postgres_triple.rs` | same insert on the Postgres backend |
| `crates/clio-store/src/sqlite_erase_purge.rs:113-161` | erase purges `item_embeddings`, `index_pending`, `items_fts`, `assoc_edges`, `memtree_nodes` — **no statement against `triples`** |
| `crates/clio-store/src/postgres_erase.rs` | same omission on Postgres |

The only `DELETE FROM triples` anywhere in the workspace is test fixture code at `crates/clio-store/src/pg_ops_tests.rs:90`.

## The content is sealed elsewhere, so this is an inconsistency, not a design choice

`crates/clio-write/src/triple.rs:246-276` builds a carrier item whose `snapshot` and `gist` contain the same SPO triple. That item **is** correctly sealed under the data-subject DEK. The identical content therefore exists twice: sealed in `items.content_ciphertext`, and in the clear in `triples`.

The `beliefs` table already documents the correct pattern in its own DDL comment at `sql/001_core.sql:335-337`:

> The proposition CONTENT is sealed under the subject DEK; only the normalized identity key and structure are plaintext (§7.4 field-level encryption).

The `triples` table applies the opposite treatment to the same kind of content. Its `subject`/`predicate`/`object` are proposition content, not bi-temporal structure.

## Reachability

`triple_add` is a first-class MCP tool.

```
crates/clio-mcp/src/write_tools.rs:279   fn triple_add(state, args)
crates/clio-mcp/src/write_tools.rs:315   clio_write::triple::triple_add(...)
crates/clio-write/src/triple.rs:210       store.commit_triple_add(admitted, &e, ...)
```

`subject`, `predicate`, and `object` are free-text arguments supplied by whatever model or user invokes the tool, so real deployments will contain whatever people type there.

## Reproduction

Driven through the real MCP tool handler, then the real erasure API. A scratch crate linked against the workspace crates by path; no repository files were modified.

```
[mcp] triple_add over the real MCP handler -> ok=true
[mcp] triples rows now: 1
[mcp]   service:hunter2Correct | runs_on | host:db-hunter2Correct.internal:5432

[erase] erase_subject ok: 1 tombstone(s) written
[erase] carrier item now: unreadable (ErasedSubject)
[erase] triples rows surviving erase: 1
[erase]   subject = service:hunter2Correct
[erase]   object  = host:db-hunter2Correct.internal:5432
[erase]   contains the secret: true
```

Real code exercised: `clio_mcp::runtime::McpState::open`, `clio_mcp::protocol::McpHandler::handle_frame`, `clio_store::SqliteStore`, `clio_store::LocalDevKms::open_persistent`, `SubjectEraseSpec` / `erase_subject`.

A second run confirmed the plaintext is present in the raw `.db` bytes on disk, and that `list_triples` returns the SPO with **no DEK present at all**.

## Impact

**Confidentiality.** Anyone with read access to the database file, a backup, a volume snapshot, or a stolen disk reads every triple in cleartext. The per-subject DEK provides no protection for this content.

**Compliance.** An erasure request is recorded as successful — tombstone written, DEK destroyed, verification probe passes — while the subject's content remains readable.

## Proposed fix

Decide the storage shape explicitly, then implement it.

- **Preferred:** seal the SPO under the subject DEK and retain only a normalized identity key in plaintext, matching the `beliefs` table design and its DDL comment.
- **Alternative:** add `triples` to the erasure purge in both `sqlite_erase_purge.rs` and `postgres_erase.rs`.

Either way, add a regression test asserting that `triple_add` followed by `erase_subject` leaves no readable copy of the content.

Note the related latent issue in the MemTree persistence primitive: `upsert_memtree_node` has no production caller today (only test fixtures), so `memtree_nodes.summary_gist` is currently a plaintext column with no reachable writer. Worth a guard test before anyone wires that primitive up.

## Related

- #24 — provider key and memory payload sent over cleartext `http://` (the in-transit counterpart to this at-rest gap)

comments.body:
This is the highest-severity finding from a read-only security audit of the repository. The full set, in severity order:

| Issue | Severity | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| #20 | High | Plaintext triple SPO survives compliance erasure (this issue) |
| #21 | Medium | Sync AEAD nonce derived from wall clock and plaintext length, not a CSPRNG |
| #22 | Medium | Sync server buffers requests unboundedly before authenticating, and handles connections serially |
| #23 | Low | MCP HTTP transport spawns unbounded threads with no read timeout |
| #24 | Low | Provider API key and memory payload sent over cleartext `http://` to any host |

**Two natural groupings:**

- **Content confidentiality** — #20 (at rest) and #24 (in transit) both leak memory content in the clear. #21 is the crypto path for sync payloads.
- **HTTP transport resource limits** — #22 and #23 share one root cause: hand-rolled HTTP servers with no size, time, or concurrency bounds. Worth fixing together.

**How these were verified.** Every finding was reproduced against real production code paths — a real `McpState` and `McpHandler`, a real `SqliteStore` with the real `LocalDevKms`, a real `sync_serve` over real TCP, and the real `SyncCipherKey::seal`. No repository file was modified; the reproductions ran from a scratch crate outside the tree. Each finding was then independently re-checked for reachability, existing mitigations, and overstated impact before inclusion — which is why several initial severity assessments were revised downward.

**Known coverage gaps in the audit**, so these issues are not read as a complete picture:

- No dependency advisory scan was possible (`cargo-audit`, `osv-scanner` and similar tools are not installed on the audit host). Third-party crate risk is unreviewed.
- PostgreSQL was not exercised; no server was available. The Postgres paths in #20 and #22 are confirmed by code and schema reading only. Both backends use parallel SQL with the same omissions.
- Codebase-memory graph indexing was unavailable, so discovery used search and direct reading rather than call-graph analysis.

title: [security:high] Plaintext triple SPO survives compliance erasure (DEK shredded, content still readable)
